Siddhāntasūktimañjarī
bibl.note: Thangaswami, R (1980). A Bibliographical Survey of Advaita Vedānta Literature. Madras: Rathnam Press.
Catalogue of the Sanskrit Manuscripts in the Library of the India Office (IO). Part I, 1887.
Notices of Sanskrit MSS by Rajendralala Mitra. Vol. II, Part I. Calcutta: Baptist Mission Press, 1872.
It has 250 verses and an auto-commentary called Prakāśa. See New Catalogus Catalogorum (NCC). Vols 1–36: vol. 5, p. 207a

This work contains the essence of Appayya Dīkṣita's Siddhāntaleśasaṃgraha. It is divided into 4 sections: Samanvaya, Avirodha, Sādhana, and Phala. (See Thangaswami, R. A Bibliographical Survey of Advaita Vedānta Literature. Madras: Rathnam Press, 1980: p. 334.)

'The author styles himself a Bhikshu, whereby he evidently means to call himself a mendicant, and not a Buddhist. He quotes most of the leading authors on the Vedanta.' (See Notices of Sanskrit MSS by Rajendralala Mitra. Vol. II, Part I. Calcutta: Baptist Mission Press, 1872: p. 3, ms. 524.)
